record.context_brief: Permanent generalization of symmetric function mean inequality
record.original_question: Fix positive vectors c,b_1,b_2,... in R^n. For a positive vector x in R^n and 1 <= r <= n, define S_{r,n}(x) as per[x repeated r times, b_1,...,b_{n-r}] divided by per[x repeated r-1 times, b_1,...,b_{n-r}, c], where per[...] is the permanent of the matrix whose displayed vectors are its columns. For any positive vectors x and y, does S_{r,n}(x+y) >= S_{r,n}(x)+S_{r,n}(y) hold?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n\ge 2$ and fix positive vectors $c, b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_{n-1} \in \mathbb{R}^n$ (i.e. vectors with strictly positive entries). For an $n\times n$ matrix $M$, let $\operatorname{per}(M)=\sum_{\sigma\in S_n}\prod_{i=1}^n M_{i,\sigma(i)}$ denote the permanent of $M$. Given column vectors $v_1,\ldots,v_n\in\mathbb{R}^n$, write $\operatorname{per}[v_1,\ldots,v_n]$ for the permanent of the matrix whose $j$-th column is $v_j$.

For an integer $r$ with $1\le r\le n$ and a positive vector $x\in\mathbb{R}^n$, define
$$S_{r,n}(x) \;=\; \frac{\operatorname{per}[\,\underbrace{x,\ldots,x}_{r\text{ times}},\,b_1,\ldots,b_{n-r}\,]}{\operatorname{per}[\,\underbrace{x,\ldots,x}_{r-1\text{ times}},\,b_1,\ldots,b_{n-r},\,c\,]}.$$

Determine whether, for every choice of positive vectors $x,y\in\mathbb{R}^n$ and every $r$ with $1\le r\le n$, the superadditivity inequality
$$S_{r,n}(x+y) \;\ge\; S_{r,n}(x) + S_{r,n}(y)$$
holds.
